rules.title: Writ scalar leaf patterns
rules.statement: Within a Writ value pattern (@{...}/@[...]), the scalar leaves are: null (`@null`), bool (`@true`/`@false`), integer (`@<int>`), and string (`@"..."`). Each tests the corresponding AnyVal scrutinee: null-ness, boolean equality, integer equality, and string equality respectively.
rules.divergence: Writ pattern matching is a Logos addition (no Rust equivalent).

rules.title: Writ integer pattern fits i24
rules.statement: A Writ integer pattern `@<int>` value v must satisfy -2^23 <= v < 2^23 (i24 range); otherwise it is a compile error. The literal may carry a negation flag that negates the parsed magnitude.
rules.divergence: Logos addition; i24 bound is Writ-specific.

rules.title: Writ map pattern
rules.statement: A Writ map pattern `@{k: p, ...}` matches iff the scrutinee is a map AND, for each listed entry key k, the key is present and its slot value matches sub-pattern p (conjunction over all entries). An entry without a value sub-pattern requires only presence of the key. Map patterns are non-exhaustive: keys not listed are ignored.

rules.title: Writ array pattern length and rest
rules.statement: A Writ array pattern `@[p0, p1, ...]` matches iff the scrutinee is an array of exactly the listed element count and each element matches its sub-pattern. A trailing `..` rest changes the length check to >= (count of non-rest elements) and binds no further elements. `..` is permitted only as the LAST element; otherwise a compile error.

rules.title: Typed Writ array pattern element types
rules.statement: A typed Writ array pattern `@<T>[..]` matches iff the scrutinee has the array type-code for element type T. T must be one of {I8,U8,I16,U16,I32,U32,I64,U64,F32,F64,AnyVal}; any other element type is a compile error.

rules.title: Typed Writ map pattern key/value types
rules.statement: A typed Writ map pattern `@<K[,V]>{..}` matches iff the scrutinee has the map type-code for key type K. K must be one of {Varchar,I32,U32,I64,U64}; the value type V, if given, must be AnyVal. Any other key or value type is a compile error.

rules.title: Named wildcard inside Writ pattern binds the AnyVal
rules.statement: A wildcard with a non-`_` name inside a Writ pattern binds that name to the current AnyVal sub-value and always matches; a `_` (or empty) name binds nothing.

rules.title: Or-patterns may not mix Writ and non-Writ alternatives
rules.statement: In an or-pattern, if any alternative is a Writ pattern then all alternatives must be Writ patterns; mixing Writ patterns with non-Writ patterns is a compile error. An all-Writ or-pattern matches iff any alternative matches (disjunction).

rules.title: `_` binding name introduces no variable
rules.statement: A binding whose name is `_` introduces no variable into scope (across variant-data, tuple, struct-field, and wildcard patterns). This prevents a phantom binding from scheduling a drop on a payload the user discarded with `_`.

rules.title: Struct pattern substitutes concrete type-args into field types
rules.statement: When matching a struct pattern against a concrete generic struct `S<A,B>`, each bound field's type is the field's declared type with the struct's type parameters substituted by the scrutinee's concrete type-args (e.g. `match s { S { x, y } }` over `S<u8,u16>` binds x:u8, y:u16). A `&`/`&mut`/`*` scrutinee is dereferenced first to obtain the type-args.

rules.title: Default binding modes for struct shorthand fields under a reference scrutinee
rules.statement: Under a `&`/`&mut` struct scrutinee, a shorthand field binding of a move-only field type T binds by reference (`&T` / `&mut T` matching the scrutinee's mutability) rather than moving the field out; Copy field types bind by value. Error and bare-TypeVar field types are excluded from the reference promotion.

rules.title: Or-pattern alternatives bind identical names and types
rules.statement: All alternatives of an or-pattern bind the same set of names with the same types; bindings are declared from the first alternative.

rules.title: Reference pattern strips one reference layer
rules.statement: A reference pattern `&p` binds its inner pattern against the pointee of a `&`/`&mut` scrutinee type; against a non-reference scrutinee the inner type is Error.

rules.title: Slice pattern element and named-rest types
rules.statement: In a slice pattern, prefix and suffix sub-patterns bind against the element type T of the scrutinee. A named rest `xs @ ..` binds the sub-slice as `&[T]` (slice type), not an element; an anonymous `..` rest binds nothing.

rules.title: `mut` binding pattern marks variable mutable
rules.statement: A wildcard-name binding written with `mut` (tracked per pattern) declares the bound variable as mutable.

rules.title: if condition must be bool
rules.statement: A non-pattern `if` condition must have type bool; Error and Never types are accepted (Never permits `if return x {}`), any other type is a compile error.

rules.title: if-let desugars to a two-arm match
rules.statement: `if let P = e { THEN } else { ELSE }` lowers to `match e { P => THEN, _ => ELSE }`, with nested-payload destructures emitted before THEN so their bindings are in scope.

rules.title: let-chain trailing condition becomes a match-arm guard
rules.statement: `if let P = e && <cond> { THEN } else { ELSE }` desugars to `match e { P if <cond> => THEN, _ => ELSE }`: the chain condition becomes an arm guard, sees the pattern's bindings, must be bool (else Error accepted), and is conjoined AFTER the pattern's own refutable guards.

rules.title: let-chain condition cannot reference nested enum-variant bindings
rules.statement: A let-chain trailing condition may reference nested tuple/struct payload bindings (re-extracted as a guard prologue) but may NOT reference bindings from a nested enum-variant payload pattern; doing so is a compile error.

rules.title: Nested refutable payload predicates gate the then-arm
rules.statement: Refutable inner patterns (nested variant/literal payload predicates) of an if-let pattern are conjoined into the then-arm guard; a predicate failure falls through to the wildcard else-arm.

rules.title: Per-branch move state merges by union over non-diverging branches
rules.statement: Across an `if`'s branches each branch is analyzed from the pre-if move state; the post-if moved set is the union of moves from all non-diverging branches (a branch ending in return/break/continue diverges and contributes nothing). A missing then/else branch behaves as a non-diverging fall-through preserving the pre-if state.

rules.title: Definite-assignment merge across if branches
rules.statement: A variable is uninitialized at the if's merge point iff it is uninitialized on ANY incoming non-diverging branch path (union of currently-uninit sets over non-diverging branches); diverging branches contribute nothing to the merge.
